qa.q: A 3-row pyramid is built on the Fibonacci numbers 1, 1, 2. What is the top?
qa.e: 1 + 2 × 1 + 2 = 5, another Fibonacci number.

qa.q: A 3-row pyramid is built on 2, 3, 5. What is the top?
qa.e: 2 + 2 × 3 + 5 = 13 — a Fibonacci number.

qa.q: A 3-row pyramid has bottom row 7, b, 9 and top 40. What is b?
A 2 × 2 calendar block adds up to 72. What is its top-left date?
qa.e: 4a + 16 = 72, so 4a = 56 and a = 14. The dates are 14, 15, 21, 22.

qa.q: A 2 × 2 calendar block adds up to 100. What is its top-left date?
A cross shape of 5 dates (centre and its 4 neighbours) adds up to 100. What is the centre date?
The 9 dates in a 3 × 3 calendar block add up to 117. What is the centre date?
qa.e: The nine dates pair up around the centre, so the total is 9c. c = 117 ÷ 9 = 13.

qa.q: In that 3 × 3 block with centre 13, what is the smallest date?
qa.e: The top-left date is 13 − 7 − 1 = 5.

qa.q: Three dates side by side in a row add up to 45. What is the smallest?
qa.e: The middle one is 45 ÷ 3 = 15, so the dates are 14, 15, 16.
Subtract the second from the first: ▲ = 14 − 9 = 5.

qa.q: Using 2, 3 and 4 once each (2-digit × 1-digit), what is the largest product?
qa.e: 32 × 4 = 128 beats 42 × 3 = 126 and every other arrangement.

qa.q: Which arrangement of 2, 3, 4 gives the largest product?
qa.e: Using the largest digit as the multiplier wins: 32 × 4 = 128.

qa.q: Using 5, 7 and 9 once each, what is the largest product?
qa.e: 75 × 9 = 675. The next best is 95 × 7 = 665.

qa.q: For digits a > b > c, what is (10b + c) × a − (10a + c) × b?
qa.e: 10ab + ac − 10ab − bc = ac − bc = c(a − b).

qa.q: Using 1, 6 and 8 once each, what is the largest product?
qa.e: 61 × 8 = 488 and 81 × 6 = 486. The rule picks 61 × 8.

qa.q: Using 2, 3 and 4 once each (2-digit × 1-digit), what is the SMALLEST product?
qa.e: 34 × 2 = 68 is smallest; 24 × 3 = 72 is next.

qa.q: Using 6, 7 and 8 once each, what is the largest product?
What is 47 + 74?
666 is divisible by 37. What is 666 ÷ 37?
Every number of the form abcabc (like 728728) is divisible by which of these?
qa.e: abcabc = abc × 1001 = abc × 7 × 11 × 13.

qa.q: A two-digit number plus its reverse is 143. What is the sum of its digits?
For the digits 2, 5 and 7, what is 257 + 572 + 725?
Solve 5x − 7 = 2x + 8. What is x?
Solve 3(x − 2) = 2x + 4. What is x?
qa.e: Expand: 3x − 6 = 2x + 4. Then 3x − 2x = 4 + 6, so x = 10. Check: 3 × 8 = 24 and 20 + 4 = 24.

qa.q: Solve x/3 + 4 = 10. What is x?
qa.e: Subtract 4: x/3 = 6. Multiply by 3: x = 18.

qa.q: Meena is 3 times as old as her brother. Together their ages add up to 32 years. How old is her brother?
qa.e: Let the brother be x. Then x + 3x = 32, so 4x = 32 and x = 8. Meena is 24.

qa.q: The sum of three consecutive numbers is 87. What is the smallest of them?
Riya has ₹50 more than Arjun. Together they have ₹290. How much does Arjun have?
qa.e: Let Arjun have x. Then x + (x + 50) = 290, so 2x = 240 and x = ₹120. Riya has ₹170.

qa.q: The length of a rectangle is 4 cm more than its width. Its perimeter is 48 cm. What is the width?
qa.e: Perimeter = 2(w + w + 4) = 4w + 8 = 48. So 4w = 40 and w = 10 cm. The length is 14 cm.

qa.q: Solve (2x + 1)/3 = (x + 4)/2. What is x?
qa.e: Multiply both sides by 6: 2(2x + 1) = 3(x + 4). So 4x + 2 = 3x + 12, and x = 10. Check: 21/3 = 7 and 14/2 = 7.

qa.q: Of all rectangles with a perimeter of 20 cm (whole-number sides), which area is the largest?
qa.e: Length + breadth = 10. The square 5 × 5 gives 25 cm², more than 6 × 4 = 24 cm².

qa.q: A 9 cm × 1 cm rectangle has the same perimeter as a 5 cm square. What is its area?
qa.e: 9 × 1 = 9 cm², much less than the square's 25 cm², even though both perimeters are 20 cm.

qa.q: Which statement about area and perimeter is true?
qa.a: Shapes with the same perimeter can have different areas
qa.e: 9 × 1 and 5 × 5 rectangles share a perimeter of 20 cm but have areas 9 and 25 cm².

qa.q: A square of side 6 cm has its side doubled. What is the new area?
qa.e: New side 12 cm, so area = 144 cm² — 4 times the old 36 cm².

qa.q: A 4 cm × 3 cm rectangle has both sides tripled. What is its new area?
qa.e: 12 × 9 = 108 cm², which is 9 times the old 12 cm².

qa.q: A 5 m × 3 m carpet has only its length doubled. What is its new area?
qa.e: 10 × 3 = 30 m² — doubling one side doubles the area.

qa.q: In how many ways can a square be divided into 4 parts of equal area?
qa.a: Many ways — strips, small squares, triangles and more
qa.e: Any split where each part has a quarter of the area works, so there are endless ways.

qa.q: How many 1 cm unit squares cover a 7 cm × 4 cm rectangle?
qa.e: 7 rows of 4 (or 4 rows of 7) = 28 unit squares, so the area is 28 cm².

qa.q: An L-shaped room is made of a 6 m × 4 m rectangle and a 3 m × 2 m rectangle. What is its total area?
A garden 20 m × 15 m has a path 2 m wide all around it on the outside. What is the area of the path?
qa.e: Outer rectangle = 24 × 19 = 456 m². Garden = 300 m². Path = 456 − 300 = 156 m².

qa.q: A 10 m × 6 m lawn has two paths, each 1 m wide, crossing in the middle and parallel to the sides. What is the total area of the paths?
qa.e: Strips: 10 × 1 = 10 and 6 × 1 = 6. The 1 m × 1 m centre is in both, so 10 + 6 − 1 = 15 m².

qa.q: A square tile 30 cm × 30 cm has a 10 cm × 10 cm square cut out of the middle. What area is left?
The front of a hut is a rectangle 8 m wide and 5 m tall, with a triangular roof of base 8 m and height 3 m on top. What is the total area?
qa.e: Rectangle = 8 × 5 = 40. Triangle = ½ × 8 × 3 = 12. Total = 52 m².

qa.q: A photo 12 cm × 8 cm has a frame 1 cm wide around it on the outside. What is the area of the frame?
qa.e: Outer size = 14 cm × 10 cm = 140 cm². Photo = 96 cm². Frame = 140 − 96 = 44 cm².

qa.q: A floor 5 m × 4 m is to be covered with square tiles of side 50 cm. How many tiles are needed?
qa.e: Each tile is 0.5 m × 0.5 m = 0.25 m². Floor = 20 m². 20 ÷ 0.25 = 80 tiles. (Or 10 tiles along by 8 tiles across.)

qa.q: A trapezium-shaped flower bed has parallel sides 6 m and 10 m and a height of 4 m. A 2 m × 2 m square fountain sits inside it. What area is left for flowers?
qa.e: Trapezium = ½ × (6 + 10) × 4 = 32 m². Fountain = 4 m². Flowers = 32 − 4 = 28 m².

qa.q: A 10 cm × 6 cm rectangle is cut along a diagonal. What is the area of each triangle?
qa.e: The rectangle is 60 cm², and the two congruent triangles each get half: 30 cm².

qa.q: A triangle has base 14 cm and height 5 cm. What is its area?
A triangle has area 24 cm². With the 8 cm side as base, what is its height?
The same triangle (area 24 cm²) uses its 6 cm side as base. What is the height now?
qa.e: 48 ÷ 6 = 8 cm. A different base gives a different height but the same area.

qa.q: An obtuse triangle has base 5 cm, and its height from the opposite vertex (falling outside the triangle) is 4 cm. What is its area?
qa.e: The formula still works: ½ × 5 × 4 = 10 cm².

qa.q: How is the height of a triangle measured for a chosen base?
qa.a: The perpendicular distance from the opposite vertex to the base line
qa.e: The height must be at right angles to the base (or its extension) and reach the opposite vertex.

qa.q: A right triangle has legs 9 cm and 4 cm. What is its area?
qa.e: The legs are perpendicular, so one is the base and the other is the height: ½ × 9 × 4 = 18 cm².

qa.q: A triangular garden has an area of 45 m² and a height of 9 m. How long is its base?
Two triangles stand on the same base and between the same two parallel lines. How do their areas compare?
qa.e: Both have the same base and the same height (the distance between the parallels), so ½ × b × h is the same.

qa.q: A triangle has a base of 10 cm, and its top vertex lies on a line parallel to the base 6 cm away. What is its area?
qa.e: Height = 6 cm (the gap between the lines), so area = ½ × 10 × 6 = 30 cm².

qa.q: A median is drawn in a triangle of area 40 cm². What is the area of each part?
qa.e: A median makes two triangles with equal bases and the same height, so each has half: 20 cm².

qa.q: The midpoints of the sides of a triangle with area 48 cm² are joined. What is the area of each small triangle?
qa.e: Joining the midpoints makes 4 congruent triangles: 48 ÷ 4 = 12 cm².

qa.q: Triangle ABC has area 60 cm². D is the midpoint of BC and E is the midpoint of AD. What is the area of triangle ABE?
qa.e: AD halves the area: ABD = 30. Then BE is a median of ABD and halves it again: ABE = 15 cm².

qa.q: A parallelogram of area 50 cm² and a triangle share a base and lie between the same parallels. What is the triangle's area?
qa.e: Triangle = ½ × b × h and parallelogram = b × h, so the triangle has half: 25 cm².

qa.q: What happens to a triangle's area if its top vertex slides along a line parallel to its base?
qa.e: The base and the height (the distance to the parallel line) do not change, so neither does the area.

qa.q: All three medians of a triangle of area 36 cm² are drawn. They make 6 small triangles. What is the area of each?
qa.e: The three medians cut the triangle into 6 triangles of equal area: 36 ÷ 6 = 6 cm².

qa.q: A trapezium has parallel sides 10 cm and 6 cm, and the distance between them is 5 cm. What is its area?
A field is a trapezium with parallel sides 30 m and 50 m and a height of 20 m. What is its area?
A trapezium has an area of 60 cm² and a height of 6 cm. One parallel side is 8 cm. How long is the other parallel side?
Why is the area of a trapezium ½ × (a + b) × h?
qa.a: Two copies fit together to make a parallelogram with base (a + b) and height h
qa.e: Turn a copy upside down and join it to the first. You get a parallelogram of area (a + b) × h, and one trapezium is half of it.

qa.q: A trapezium-shaped window has parallel sides 1.2 m and 0.8 m, and a height of 1 m. What is its area?
Which length is the 'height' of a trapezium?
qa.a: The perpendicular distance between the parallel sides
qa.e: The height must be measured at right angles to the parallel sides. A slanting side is longer than the height.

qa.q: A parallelogram has a base of 14 cm and a height of 9 cm. What is its area?
qa.e: Area of a parallelogram = base × height = 14 × 9 = 126 cm².

qa.q: Joseph's trapezium has parallel sides 9 cm and 15 cm, and a height of 8 cm. He splits it with a diagonal into two triangles. What is the total area?
qa.e: Triangle 1: ½ × 9 × 8 = 36. Triangle 2: ½ × 15 × 8 = 60. Total 96 cm², the same as ½ × (9 + 15) × 8.

qa.q: A rhombus has diagonals 10 cm and 8 cm. What is its area?
qa.e: Area = ½ × 10 × 8 = 40 cm².

qa.q: In quadrilateral ABCD, diagonal AC = 12 cm. The perpendiculars from B and D to AC are 4 cm and 6 cm. What is the area of ABCD?
qa.e: Area = ½ × d × (h₁ + h₂) = ½ × 12 × 10 = 60 cm². It is two triangles: 24 + 36.

qa.q: A rhombus has an area of 96 cm² and one diagonal of 16 cm. How long is the other diagonal?
qa.e: ½ × 16 × d = 96, so 8d = 96 and d = 12 cm.

qa.q: A square has a diagonal of 6 cm. What is its area?
qa.e: A square is a rhombus with equal diagonals: ½ × 6 × 6 = 18 cm².

qa.q: Aisha's rangoli is a regular hexagon split into 6 equal triangles, each with an area of 15 cm². What is the area of the hexagon?
qa.e: 6 triangles × 15 cm² = 90 cm².

qa.q: A pentagon is split into a rectangle of area 48 cm² and a triangle of area 12 cm². What is the area of the pentagon?
qa.e: The parts do not overlap, so add them: 48 + 12 = 60 cm².

qa.q: Kabir's paper kite has diagonals of 30 cm and 20 cm. What is its area?
qa.e: The diagonals of a kite are perpendicular, so area = ½ × 30 × 20 = 300 cm².

qa.q: A rhombus has a side of 13 cm and a height of 10 cm. What is its area?
qa.e: A rhombus is a parallelogram, so area = base × height = 13 × 10 = 130 cm².

qa.q: A square of side 8 cm is cut into tangram pieces and rearranged into a cat shape. What is the cat's area?
qa.e: Rearranging pieces keeps the area: 8 × 8 = 64 cm².

qa.q: Asha must cross a rectangular park 40 m long and 30 m wide, from one corner to the opposite corner. Walking along two edges is 70 m. How many metres does she save by walking straight along the diagonal?
qa.e: The diagonal is √(40² + 30²) = √2500 = 50 m. So she saves 70 − 50 = 20 m. The straight path is the shortest.

qa.q: For an 8 × 2 rectangle, what is ((8 + 2)/2)² − ((8 − 2)/2)²?
qa.e: 5² − 3² = 25 − 9 = 16, which equals 8 × 2.

qa.q: A 6 cm × 4 cm rectangle is turned into a triangle of the same area with height 4 cm. What is the triangle's base?
qa.e: Area = 24 cm². ½ × b × 4 = 24 gives b = 12 cm — double the rectangle's length.

A rangoli is made of 4 congruent triangles, each with base 0.5 m and height 0.5 m. What is its total area?
qa.e: Each triangle: ½ × 0.5 × 0.5 = 0.125 m². Four of them: 0.5 m².

Why did the Śulba-sūtras give rules for changing shapes while keeping area?
qa.a: To build fire altars of exact sizes in different shapes
qa.e: Altars had to keep a fixed area while changing shape, so builders needed area-preserving rules.
